title: The Keeper's Last Night
synopsis: A lighthouse keeper on a storm-cut island keeps the lamp burning through the night her station is to be closed. A synthetic test story: a fixed protagonist, one supporting character with an entrance condition, dynamic characters allowed within guidance, a permitted perspective switch, and two distinct speaking voices.
visual_style: Cold coastal drama on 35 mm film grain in blue-hour light; wet stone, brass and salt-streaked glass; natural light from the lamp and the sky.
visual_anchor: Cold coastal drama on 35 mm film grain, blue-hour light, wet stone and brass.

narrator.tone: Spare, weathered, the voice of someone remembering the night years later. Never explains what the picture shows.
narrator.guidance: Between the storm's surges and at scene boundaries; never over a character's line.

world_constraints: The storm does not stop before dawn.
No one arrives by boat before the lamp fails; after that, anyone who comes has come through the storm.
narrative_premise: The last night of a lighthouse: the keeper will not leave while ships are out, and her nephew has come to make her.
long_term_narrative: The lamp fails and is mended more than once; each time, someone from the sea or the village is drawn to the light.
short_term_narrative: Open on Mara alone in the lamp room, the storm rising, the lamp turning.
thread_guidance: The question of whether Mara leaves runs the whole film; smaller setups (a failing part, a ship's light) resolve within a scene or two.

storyteller.values: This story is about what people sacrifice for duty, and whether the thing they are protecting is the duty itself or the love underneath it.
truths: Mara loves the lighthouse more than she loves being happy.
The sea is indifferent, never malicious.
Tomas is kind underneath his impatience.
The lamp is the only thing standing between the ships and the rocks.
boundaries: This story never explains. It shows.
Violence is consequence, never spectacle — only the sea acts with force.
No cheap reversals or twists for shock.
Humor is dry and rare — Mara is funny when she is not trying to be.
storyteller.temperament: When something unexpected arrives, slow down and let the characters react honestly before the story moves. When the viewer wants spectacle, give them beauty instead — the lamp beam cutting through rain, the sea hitting the rocks. When they want answers, give them a better question. Absorb the impulse, not the literal words.

cast_policy.dynamic_guidance: Only adults from the sea or the village: sailors, fishermen, the harbourmaster. Never children, never anyone in uniform from the mainland.

perspective.switching: Only while Mara looks through the telescope, and back to third-person when she lowers it.
